title: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties
abstract: Crystal graph convolutional neural networks represent periodic crystals directly as graphs of atoms and bonds. The learned representation supports prediction of formation energy, band gap, Fermi energy, bulk modulus, shear modulus, and Poisson ratio and enables screening of materials candidates.

title: Graph Networks as a Universal Machine Learning Framework for Molecules and Crystals
abstract: MEGNet models encode atoms, bonds, and global state attributes in a graph network. Transfer learning from formation energies improves data-limited predictions, while learned elemental embeddings provide chemically meaningful structure for molecular and crystalline property prediction.

title: Benchmarking Materials Property Prediction Methods: The Matbench Test Set and Automatminer Reference Algorithm
abstract: Matbench defines standardized materials-property datasets, train-test splits, and evaluation metrics. It supports reproducible comparison of machine-learning methods across regression and classification tasks and highlights the importance of leakage-resistant evaluation.

title: Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network for Improved Materials Property Predictions
abstract: ALIGNN alternates message passing on atomistic graphs and their line graphs to incorporate bond-angle information. The architecture improves predictions for multiple crystal and molecular properties while retaining an atomistic representation suitable for candidate screening.
